chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Ashʿarī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Nothing invalidates wudu (ablution) except a state of hadath, and sleep is a state of hadath.

key_terms.النَّوْمُ: sleep, identified here as a nullifier of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification required for acts such as salat
key_terms.حَدَثٌ: a state of ritual occurrence that nullifies wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: invalidates or breaks in a legal sense

ai.seo_question: Does sleep invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle concerning wudu (ablution): it is only invalidated by hadath. It then clarifies that sleep is included among the states that invalidate wudu (ablution), making it relevant to rulings of ritual purity and worship.
